newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end little changed ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end little changed ahead of report.

text.p: Traders generally kept on the sidelines and light evening of positions dominated CME live and feeder cattle futures as market watchers awaited Friday's monthly Cattle-on-Feed report, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.175 cent per lb lower to 0.025 higher with June off 0.100 at 64.500 cents. August also ended 0.100 lower at 63.725 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.050 lower to 0.050 higher with August off 0.050 at 77.225 cents.
Evening ahead of Friday's monthly USDA data accounted for most of the action as cattle pits shrugged off bullish spillover influence from sharply lower pork complex futures, traders said.

Lower boxed beef prices provided pressure at times, but many traders said they expect beef values to bottom soon after falling to lowest levels since late February. Packer willingness to hold cash cattle prices at $63 per cwt earlier in the week also curbed declines in nearbys. The outlook for tighter fed cattle supplies later in the year boosted deferred months at times, sources noted.
Futures and cash cattle markets alike, were expected to be quiet again Friday ahead of the report, which will be released at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT.

Analyst estimates on the report put June 1 total on-feed cattle supplies in the major seven states at an average of 113.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 111.5 to 114 percent. A number at the high end would be a record high. Placement estimates averaged 117.2 in a range of 110.5 to 124 percent and marketings averaged 99 in a range of 97 to 100.5 percent.

Refco sold June early along with local spreaders before finding mixed support, traders said. RBH, R.J. O'Brien and E.D.&F. Man sold August with local buying providing later support and limiting selling pressure from Refco and Cargill Investor Services near the close, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought August 68 calls early and bought 66 calls late. Commercials sold August 62 and 63 puts and October 64 puts, pit souces added.
Feeder cattle futures showed early strength on support from lower corn futures but also drifted back as traders evened positions ahead of the report, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index dipped $0.06 to $77.22 per cwt.
Cargill Investor Services bought August early while Dean Witter and Smith Barney sold, floor sources said.
Locals then accounted for much of the trade into the close, pit sources said.
